Property.name: Filename
Property.Description:
Name of file to output the document(s) to. May include timestamp specifiers. The %f specifier if present will be replaced with the name of the document's original filename (stripped of illegal characters).

See the method Ens.Util.File.CreateTimestamp() for documentation of timestamping options.

Property.name: TempFilename
Property.Description: Name of a temporary file to output the document(s) to. Upon completion of the upload the file with this name to the FTP server it is renamed to the name specified in the Filename setting. If this setting is blank no temporary file will be used.<p/> May include timestamp specifiers. The %f specifier if present will be replaced with the name of the document's original filename (stripped of illegal characters).<p/> See the method Ens.Util.File.CreateTimestamp() for documentation of timestamping options.

Property.name: FilePermissions
Property.Description:
Enter the file permissions, in the format entities+permissions given the following:

entities can be one or more of: u = user (owner); g=group; o=others
permissions can be one or more of: r = read; w=write; x=execute

Multiple entries should be comma-delimited. Permissions not specifically granted will be lost. For example, if you do not give users execute access, they will not have it, even if they had it before.

If FilePermissions value is blank or invalid, the permissions will not be changed from their default value.

EXAMPLES (values in parenthesis are the chmod values for the same permissions):

ugo+rwx -- Gives full access: read, write and execute to all (777)

ugo+rw -- Gives read and write (but not execute) access to all (666)

u+rwx -- Give full access to owner, no access to group and other (700)

ug+rw -- Gives read and write to owner and group; NO access to others (660)

u+rwx,go+r -- Give full access to owner, read-only to group and other (744)

ug+rw,o+x -- gives read/write to the file owner and group, but execute-only to others (661)

ugo+r -- gives read-only access to all (444)

ug+rw,o+x -- gives read/write to the file owner and group, but only execute-only to others (661)

u+x -- Give execute only to user, group and others have no access (100)

Property.name: ActionOnTargetFile
Property.Description:
This is the action to be taken on the target file AFTER it has been moved. If you are simply SFTPing the file and don't need to do anything after that, leave this field blank.

If the file needs to be renamed, include the full absolute path to the new location including the new file name.

NOTE: The following special values can also be included in the new file names:
%f - The original filename of the file
%CD - The date the file was processed in format 1970-01-01
%CT - The time the file was processed in format 12:00:00AM
%# - The current sequence number

EXAMPLE: Setting this value to %f_%CD_%CT_%# would rename testfile to something like

testfile_08/07/2015_02:39:23PM_1

Property.name: valueToBeReplaced
Property.Description: Property to store the values to be replaced

Property.name: StartingSequenceNumber
Property.Description: This is the value the sequence number is set to each time the component is restarted

Property.name: MinimumSequenceNumber
Property.Description: This is the lowest value the sequence number can have. If the sequence number is below this value and the SequenceIncrement is less than zero, the sequence number is reset to the MaximumSequenceNumber. If the sequence number is less than the MinimumSequenceNumber and the SequenceIncrement is greater than zero, the sequence number is set to the MinimumSequenceNumber. If MinimumSequenceNumber is set to be more than the MaximumSequenceNumber, the sequence number will be set to zero.

Property.name: MaximumSequenceNumber
Property.Description: This is the highest value the sequence number can have. If the sequence number is above this value and the SequenceIncrement is greater than zero, the sequence number is reset to the MinimumSequenceNumber. If the sequence number is higher than the MaximumSequenceNumber and the SequenceIncrement is less than zero, the sequence number is set to the MaximumSequenceNumber. If MaximumSequenceNumber is set to be less than the MinimumSequenceNumber, the sequence number will be set to zero.

Property.name: SequenceIncrement
Property.Description: This is how much we add to the sequence number every time we get a new event. This value can be set negative, which will result in a descending sequence number. If this value is set to zero, the sequence number will not change.

Property.name: ResetSequenceOnRestart
Property.Description: Enable ResetSequenceOnRestart if you want to reset the sequence number to the StartingSequenceNumber when this operation is restart. Be aware this could cause multiple files to have the same sequence number.

Method.name: OnMessage
ResetSequenceNumber
VerifySequenceNumber
IncrementSequenceNumber
Method.Implementation:
Set PreIncrementedSequenceNumber = ^ItfGlobal(..%ConfigName, "CurrentSequenceNumber") Set ^ItfGlobal(..%ConfigName, "CurrentSequenceNumber") = ^ItfGlobal(..%ConfigName, "CurrentSequenceNumber") + ..SequenceIncrement
$$$TRACE("Sequence Number has been incremented from "_PreIncrementedSequenceNumber_" to "_^ItfGlobal(..%ConfigName, "CurrentSequenceNumber"))
Do ..VerifySequenceNumber()

Method.name: replaceWithParticularFormat
Method.Implementation: Set key = "" For { Set ReplaceVal = ..valueToBeReplaced.GetNext(.key) Set SubBody = $REPLACE(SubBody,key,ReplaceVal) Quit:key="" } $$$TRACE("Done with replacement; SubBody="_SubBody) Quit SubBody
